regularization.skip_reason: only 2 of 4 campaign(s) fit a uniform grid; regularizing just those would leave the bundle with two sampling regimes split across train/test, so none were regularized

decision.rationale: Splitting at collection pauses produced 4 campaigns, but only 2 fit a grid (campaign(s) [3, 4] stayed too sparse). Gridding only some of them would leave one bundle carrying two sampling regimes, and the chronological train/test split would put them on opposite sides — training on gridded data and scoring on irregular data. A consistent timeline is worth more than a partial grid, so none were regularized.
alternatives: timeline.require_all_segments: false — grid the campaigns that fit and accept a mixed-regime bundle (only safe with a split that keeps both regimes on both sides)
a smaller timeline.segment_gap_seconds — splits further; helps only when the sparsity comes from pauses rather than within-campaign bursts
a coarser base_dt for this dataset — trades burst resolution for a denser grid

segments.skip_reason: regularizing onto a 40.5s grid would leave 92.6% of 8383 grid points empty, above the 80.0% threshold; the bundle keeps the original irregular timeline and is NOT on a uniform grid

decision.rationale: A uniform 40.5s grid would need 8,383 points to hold 623 observations — 92.6% of the grid would be synthetic, over the 80% budget. Imputing that much invented structure would dominate the real signal, so the original irregular timestamps were kept.
alternatives: timeline.segment_regularization: true — split at collection pauses so each campaign gets its own grid (often the whole cause of the sparsity)
a coarser base_dt (> 40.5s) — fewer grid points, but short-interval structure is averaged away
raise validation.sparse_skip_pct above 93 — accepts a mostly-synthetic grid; only sensible if the model is meant to fill it
